newsitem.title: USA: Century Aluminum invests in plate capacity.
newsitem.headline: Century Aluminum invests in plate capacity.

text.p: Century Aluminum will spend $28 million on doubling heat-treated plate capacity to meet strong growth in aerospace manufacture, the company said in a statement.
"The timing of the expansion coincides with surging growth in world markets for plate, especially aerospace," said Gerald Meyers, Century's president and chief operating officer.
"Our studies indicate that demand for heat-treated aluminum plate in all markets will grow nearly 30 percent by 2000," Meyers added.

The project will create 40 new jobs at the company's Ravenswood, West Virginia plant. Work on the expansion will start immediately and be completed in phases with the first start-up beginning in the first quarter of 1998.
A Century spokesman told Reuters that Ravenswood's current heat-treated plate capacity was 25 million pounds per year. All the extra 25 million pounds of capacity will be on stream in early 1999.
No firm decision has been taken as to how the investment money will be raised. "We think we can do it internally," the spokesman said.
California-based Century said the two other main players in the U.S. aerospace heat-treated plate market were Alcoa and Reynolds Metals
Meyers also expected greater use of heat-treated plate in manufacturing machine tools and molds for making plastic parts, and to replace high-cost forged aluminum parts in some applications.
